exposure: Objective indication (all other indications for cesarean delivery)
Subjective indication (non-reassuring fetal heart tracing and arrest of labor disorders)
cohort: 620 women (296 White, 324 Micronesian) who underwent cesarean delivery at the largest maternity hospital in Hawai'i
finding: Micronesian women had significantly higher odds of cesarean delivery due to a subjective indication compared to White women, suggesting that factors beyond medical necessity, possibly provider bias, may contribute to racial/ethnic disparities in cesarean delivery.
mod_finding: The study found a disparity in cesarean delivery rates based on subjective indications, which may reflect bias in decision-making regarding mode of delivery.
